instruction: The touchpad is too sensitive and I keep accidentally clicking things. Can you disable tap-to-click on the touchpad?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling tap-to-click on touchpad via gsettings. The setup enables tap-to-click, and the task asks the user to disable it. Evaluator verifies the setting is changed to false using exact_match metric with vm_command_line getter.
metadata.verification: Verified by checking gsettings touchpad tap-to-click pattern - the setting is a boolean that should be toggled from true to false.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: vm_command_line executes 'gsettings get' to read the current tap-to-click setting
Metric logic is correct: exact_match appropriately compares the result string with expected value
Expected value is correct: 'false\n' matches the gsettings output format and correctly represents disabled tap-to-click
Complete instruction coverage: evaluator verifies the single requirement (disable tap-to-click)
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts setting value -> metric compares with expected 'false\n'
Practical feasibility: gsettings is command-line based, no UI dependencies, no postconfig needed
Proper edge case handling: exact_match will fail if setting remains 'true\n' or command fails
